name: Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPP Investments)
headquarters: Toronto, Ontario, Canada (One Queen Street East, Suite 2500 on SEC 13F covers; 141 Bay Street, Suite 3100 on 2026 EDGAR filings); offices in Hong Kong, London, Mumbai, New York, São Paulo and Sydney

ownership.ticker: No listed equity — a federal Crown corporation created by the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board Act (1997, c. 40), accountable to Parliament and to the federal and provincial finance ministers; funds itself with debt (SEC CIK 0001283718; fiscal year ends 31 March)
ownership.notes: CPP Investments describes itself as 'an independent Crown Corporation' that 'operates at arm's length from governments'; its objects under the Act are to invest 'with a view to achieving a maximum rate of return, without undue risk of loss, having regard to the factors that may affect the funding of the CPP'. A special examination is required every six years (last: Deloitte, February 2022). It manages two accounts — base CPP and additional CPP (contributions since January 2019). Results are published quarterly (mid-August, mid-November, mid-February and about 21 May); no sell-side consensus exists, so every `expected` field below is empty and performance is measured against the Fund's own benchmark portfolios.

summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** CPP Investments is the corpus's largest single pool of capital that signs for no equipment and the one with the most control positions behind the buyers: it is 'the majority shareholder' of Pattern Energy (69.1% together with other institutional investors after folding its wholly owned Cordelio into Pattern on 2 April 2026), 40% owner of ALLETE and Minnesota Power with GIP (closed 15 December 2025 at USD 67 a share, USD 6.2bn including debt), the c. 51% controlling owner of atNorth since 2 September 2026 (USD 1.3bn; Equinix c. 34%, Partners Group c. 10%; USD 4bn enterprise value — the 60% / USD 1.6bn signing term was re-cut by rollover), a 37.5% controlling partner in Equinix's more-than-USD 15bn US xScale venture, 12% of AirTrunk beside Blackstone and 50% of Inkia (Peru, USD 3.4bn EV, closed 8 June 2026). Its ~13% indirect interest in Sempra Infrastructure Partners beside KKR (USD 3.0bn) had not closed in any filing through 21 August 2026. Net assets were C$793.3bn at 31 March 2026 (7.8% net return; the benchmark portfolios returned 13.2%) and C$863.6bn at 30 June 2026 (7.5% in the quarter, the strongest in more than a decade). It sold 2,660,479 Constellation shares on 2 June 2026 (Calpine proceeds; 1.3% retained) and launched a C$50bn Maple Fund with Brookfield for Canadian infrastructure on 15 September 2026.

**BACKGROUND.** Per its own releases and the fiscal 2025 annual report, the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board manages the CPP Fund through six departments; the AI-infrastructure and power positions sit in Real Assets (C$146.7bn at 31 March 2025; Infrastructure C$62.0bn; Sustainable Energies about C$36.3bn), led by Max Biagosch with James Bryce (Infrastructure) and Bill Rogers (Sustainable Energies). Fiscal 2026 reclassified its energy holdings from private and public equities into Real Assets, which returned 12.2% that year per press accounts. Infrastructure Investor ranks CPP Investments fourth among institutional infrastructure investors (USD 40,058m allocation, July 2026); Global SWF ranks it 18th among all sovereign and public funds (USD 608bn) with a 10/10 governance score. Canadian investments were C$119.2bn at fiscal year-end against a US share of about 47%, the fact behind the domestic-investment pressure from Ottawa and the Senate.
ecosystemRole: We assess CPP Investments as the capital segment's quiet incumbent: it ranks fourth globally in infrastructure allocation and holds controlling or co-controlling positions in a regulated utility (ALLETE), a renewables and transmission developer (Pattern, with SunZia), a Nordic data-centre platform (atNorth) and the US xScale programme, yet it issues no equipment order itself and appears in no Senate letter. The buyers are its platforms — Pattern's project companies, Minnesota Power's rate base, atNorth's campuses, the xScale JV's builds — and the strategics it co-owns with (Equinix, GIP, KKR, Blackstone). Two features distinguish it from the asset managers in this segment: it invests its own pension capital rather than fee-paying third-party money, so it has no fund clock and no exit obligation (it has held Pattern since 2020 and consolidated Cordelio into it rather than selling), and it reports quarterly against a benchmark rather than a consensus. For a seller, CPP is the counterparty that decides whether a platform is funded for its next build — and increasingly the lender too, through Real Assets Credit (a C$225m construction loan for a Cambridge, Ontario hyperscale data centre; CoreWeave facilities).

productsAndServices.name: Real Assets — Infrastructure, Real Estate and Sustainable Energies (the department that holds the power and data-centre positions)
productsAndServices.category: Investment department — direct infrastructure, energy and property equity
productsAndServices.description: Real Assets 'invests in real estate, infrastructure, as well as both conventional and renewable energy assets globally'. Per the fiscal 2025 annual report it held net assets of C$146.7bn at 31 March 2025 with 270 FTEs, a five-year net return of 7.0% and ten-year value added of 2.2% a year 'with sustainable energies as the largest contributor'; the asset-class view showed Infrastructure at C$62.0bn and Real Estate at C$48.5bn. Three groups sit inside it: Infrastructure (James Bryce — Tarchon, FCC Enviro, toll roads), Real Estate, and Sustainable Energies (Bill Rogers — Pattern and Cordelio, Inkia, Calpine, Aera, Wolf Midstream, Octopus), the group created on 6 April 2021 by merging Energy & Resources with Power & Renewables and holding about C$36.3bn at 31 March 2025. Fiscal 2026 reclassified the energies holdings previously reported inside private and public equities into the Real Assets asset class. Net investments of the department were C$142.4bn at 30 June 2025 (Q1 fiscal 2026 deck); the fiscal 2026 annual report, which carries the 31 March 2026 department figures, could not be located as a PDF from this environment.
highlights: Platforms it controls or co-controls: Pattern Energy (majority; 69.1% with other institutional investors), ALLETE (40%, with GIP), atNorth (c. 51%), Equinix xScale US JV (37.5%), Inkia (50%), Tarchon interconnector (majority, C$1bn, closing end-2026), Reventus Power (wholly owned offshore wind), Cordelio Power (wholly owned until sold to Pattern for shares, 2 April 2026)

productsAndServices.name: Canadian programmes — the Maple Fund with Brookfield and the domestic-investment response
productsAndServices.description: On 15 September 2026, at the first Canada Investment Summit, CPP Investments and Brookfield Asset Management launched the Maple Fund: up to C$50bn of equity, 50/50, up to C$25bn each over an initial five years, for projects of more than C$5bn of equity in 'critical infrastructure and strategic industries across Canada', open to third-party co-investors and 'incremental to normal-course' investing. The same day John Graham told the summit 'We are not required to invest in Canada. We invest here when an opportunity earns its place on a risk return basis.' Canadian investments stood at C$119.2bn at 31 March 2026.
highlights: Context: Fall Economic Statement 2024 (repeal of the 30% rule; an AI data-centre programme matching pension capital 1:2 up to C$15bn), Budget 2025's C$1tn target, quarterly Finance Minister meetings with the Maple 8, and Senate Finance chair Carignan's call for a legislated mandate (May 2026)
productsAndServices.positioning: CPP's answer to the mandate debate: a voluntary, scaled vehicle rather than a statutory allocation.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Co-investment partnership with Brookfield; third-party co-investors invited.

strategyRead: **(High confidence)** We assess that **CPP Investments is a directory of buyers with no exit clock**: it signs no equipment order, but its platforms do, and because it invests pension capital rather than a fund it holds and consolidates (Pattern since 2020, Cordelio folded in for shares) where a manager would sell. Basis: Pattern's and Cordelio's releases; CPP's 69.1% statement; the absence of any sale, secondary or IPO report on Pattern through 2026. A seller to Pattern or Minnesota Power is selling to a CPP-funded balance sheet that will still be there at the next build.

**(High confidence)** We assess that **the atNorth re-cut from 60% to c. 51% is the model of how CPP's headline terms move**: the signing release stated about USD 1.6bn for about 60%, the completion release c. 51% for USD 1.3bn after Partners Group reinvested for c. 10% and insiders rolled equity. Basis: the two joint releases of 27 February and 2 September 2026. Read every CPP percentage against the completion document, not the agreement.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **CPP's data-centre exposure is now wider than any single investor's in this corpus but is held mostly without control** — xScale (37.5%), Goodman Europe (50% of a partnership), EQT/EdgeConneX (undisclosed), CtrlS (8.2% plus a 48% JV), Japan DC Partners (an LP commitment), Vantage and Yondr (commitments), AirTrunk (12%), the Korean JVs — with atNorth the one controlling position. Basis: CPP's own releases and quarterly summaries. For a seller that means CPP is rarely the decision-maker on a campus's equipment; Equinix, Goodman, EdgeConneX and Blackstone are.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **the Sempra Infrastructure Partners stake is the position most likely to be reported wrongly**, because three documents give three framings: CPP (~13% indirect for ~USD 3.0bn), Sempra's 10-Q (a KKR-led 'KKR Partners' buying 45% for ~USD 9.99bn, CPPIB an 'indirect co-investor') and the corpus's KKR dossier (USD 10bn for 45%, USD 31.7bn EV). All three are consistent; none states closing. Sempra expected Q3 2026 and tied its CFO succession to it; no completion appeared in filings through 21 August 2026.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **Ottawa's domestic-investment pressure will shape CPP's next infrastructure allocations more than any US regulator will**: the Maple Fund (C$50bn with Brookfield) was launched on the day the CEO told the Canada Investment Summit CPP is 'not required to invest in Canada', the Senate Finance chair favours a legislated mandate, and Bill C-30 cuts base contributions from 2027. Basis: CPP's and the Prime Minister's releases; the Globe and Mail. Cuts against: CPP's governance score (10/10, Global SWF) and the two-thirds-of-provinces amendment threshold make a statutory mandate slow.

**(Low confidence)** We assess that **the fiscal 2026 benchmark miss (7.8% against 13.2%) will push CPP toward more private infrastructure, not less** — the department that outperformed was Real Assets (12.2%), and Graham attributed the miss to public-market concentration. Basis: press accounts of the results call. Treat as a tendency, not a plan.

**INDICATORS TO WATCH** — *Sempra 8-K on the Sempra Infrastructure Partners closing:* confirms CPP's ~13% and the USD 3.0bn; a termination notice after the twelve-month long-stop would reverse it. *Mid-November 2026, Q2 fiscal 2027 results:* the transaction list is where CPP discloses platform moves (watch for Tarchon closing, Maple Fund deployments, further Constellation sales). *Pattern Energy's next step — a SunZia-scale financing, a sale, or an IPO:* any would test the 'no exit clock' judgment. *The ReNew scheme vote and UK court sanction:* CPP's second take-private of a renewables IPP. *Minnesota Power's first rate case after the one-year freeze (2027):* the regulatory cost of co-owning a utility. *Any CPPIB Act amendment bill or a Senate committee report recommending a mandate.*

relationships.scale: 'the majority shareholder'; 69.1% together with other institutional investors after Cordelio (2 April 2026)
relationships.note: CPP took Pattern Energy private in 2020 (USD 26.75 a share, about USD 6.1bn enterprise value including net debt) and in April 2026 folded its wholly owned Cordelio Power into Pattern for shares.
relationships.context:
The joint release of 4 November 2019 records the all-cash agreement at USD 26.75 per share, 'implying an enterprise value of approximately $6.1 billion, including net debt'. CPP's Q3 fiscal 2026 release (13 February 2026) states that the share-based Cordelio sale 'will increase our existing ownership stake in Pattern Energy, together with other institutional investors, to 69.1% upon closing' — the percentage is the combined institutional stake, not CPP alone; Pattern's completion release of 2 April 2026 calls CPP 'the majority shareholder'. A consortium headed by APG (for ABP) and Australian Retirement Trust bought Riverstone's stake in 2025 and is described as an owner 'alongside' CPP and management.

The `pattern-energy` dossier carries the same 69.1% sentence and the same ambiguity; this dossier adds CPP's own wording.

relationships.scale: ALLETE: CPP 40% beside GIP (closed 15 December 2025; USD 6.2bn including debt)
relationships.note: CPP Investments and BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners jointly took ALLETE private; CPP states its stake as 40%.
relationships.context: CPP's fiscal 2025 release describes the agreement 'to jointly acquire ALLETE, Inc. alongside Global Infrastructure Partners for US$6.2 billion, including the assumption of debt' with CPP's stake at 40% on closing; ALLETE's 8-K of 15 December 2025 records completion at USD 67 a share in cash, about USD 200m of customer benefits, and a majority-independent board. GIP's 60% split (40% GIP V plus 20% a GIP-managed CalPERS vehicle) and 'governance shared equally' appear in the `blackrock` dossier from ALLETE's proxy; they are not stated in any CPP, ALLETE 8-K, MPUC or Senate document read for this dossier.

policyExposure.regime: Canada Pension Plan Investment Board Act (1997) — mandate, governance and the domestic-investment debate
policyExposure.exposure: The Act sets CPP's sole objective (maximum return without undue risk, having regard to CPP funding), arm's-length governance, accountability to Parliament and the finance ministers, and a six-yearly special examination; amendment requires the federal government plus two-thirds of the provinces with two-thirds of the population. Since the Fall Economic Statement of December 2024 (repeal of the 30% rule; an AI data-centre programme matching pension capital up to C$15bn), Budget 2025's C$1tn target, quarterly Finance Minister meetings with the Maple 8, the Senate Finance chair's call for a legislated mandate (May 2026) and the Canadian Shield Institute's proposed 3% mandate (September 2026), domestic allocation is the live political question; Canadian investments were C$119.2bn (about 12%) at 31 March 2026 against about 47% in the US.
policyExposure.mitigation: The C$50bn Maple Fund with Brookfield (15 September 2026); Graham: 'We invest here when an opportunity earns its place on a risk return basis.'

policyExposure.regime: Minnesota PUC and FERC §203 — ALLETE / Minnesota Power
policyExposure.exposure: The ALLETE take-private closed only after the Minnesota PUC's unanimous approval (3 October 2025; written order December) over an administrative law judge's recommendation to reject it, with conditions: a one-year base-rate freeze, ROE reduced from 9.78% to 9.65% with a 9.78% cap to 2030, USD 50m of rate credits, funding of a USD 5bn five-year capital plan, USD 50m for clean firm power and Minnesota-based independent directors; FERC approved the transfer in December 2024. Senators Warren, Sanders and Blumenthal's December 2025 letter to BlackRock about the deal names CPP only in the docket title.

policyExposure.regime: US Senate Banking Committee oversight — private-equity ownership of utilities and data centres
policyExposure.exposure: The June 2026 Warren letters on data-centre ownership went to KKR, BlackRock, Brookfield and Blackstone and the September 2026 bipartisan letter to FERC concerns GIP/AES; CPP Investments — co-owner of ALLETE, AirTrunk and atNorth and partner in the xScale venture — is not a recipient and is not named.

policyExposure.regime: Canada Pension Plan contribution rates — Bill C-30 and the Chief Actuary's reports
policyExposure.exposure: The 32nd Actuarial Report (valuation at 31 December 2024; revised version tabled 27 May 2026) finds the base and additional CPP sustainable at legislated rates, with minimum contribution rates of 9.21%/9.19% against the statutory 9.9%; Bill C-30 cuts the base rate to 9.5% from 1 January 2027, which press accounts put at about 4% lower contributions from 2027. Net transfers into the Fund were C$22.0bn in fiscal 2026.

policyExposure.regime: Australian Foreign Investment Review Board and UK/German regulatory approvals
policyExposure.exposure: The AirTrunk acquisition was conditional on FIRB approval (completed 23 December 2024); the Tarchon interconnector is 'a regulated asset progressing through the relevant regulatory approvals process in the UK and Germany' with completion expected end-2026; the ReNew take-private proceeds under a UK Companies Act Part 26 scheme requiring 75% approval and court sanction.

policyExposure.regime: Litigation — climate-risk duty (Ecojustice) and the FNZ class action
policyExposure.exposure: Four young Canadians sued CPPIB on 27 October 2025 alleging breach of duties of impartiality and even-handedness in managing climate risk, after CPP's 2025 reversal of its net-zero commitment; separately, a USD 4.6bn New Zealand employee class action against FNZ names CPP Investments and CDPQ among controlling investors (first hearing 12 May 2026). CPP expanded its portfolio carbon-footprint reporting in August 2026 (86.7% of C$787bn below 40 tCO2e per USD m EVIC).
